conventions.convention: Invariance means πK=π on every measurable set; on a countable discrete space, π(y)=Σx π(x)p(x,y). No irreducibility or uniqueness is implicit.
The positive return time starts at n=1; occupation and ergodic sums include time zero. Null recurrence is defined only for recurrent states.
Total variation distance is supA |μ(A)−ν(A)|, hence half the sum of absolute singleton-mass differences on a countable discrete space.
The process definition uses real or complex values, the one-sided path space indexed by nonnegative integers, and the left shift. Ergodicity uses strictly invariant measurable events.
Specht modules are spans of signed column antisymmetrizers applied to tabloids over a commutative ring; signs are images of integer signs. The empty Specht module is the ground ring.
Removable corners are ordered from top to bottom, r1<⋯<rm. Restriction fixes the largest label n, and the filtration spans standard polytabloids with n in the first i removable rows.
The tensor place action is a left action with the inverse permutation on positions. The linear action is diagonal, and Δ(T) is the sum of T over tensor positions; the zeroth tensor power is C.
For left Haar measure, right translation by h scales integration by ΔG(h)−1, and rho covariance is ρ(xh)=ΔH(h)ΔG(h)−1ρ(x).
Pushforward under the left action is g*μ(E)=μ(g−1E). Strong quasi-invariance requires jointly continuous positive densities; rho-derived density is ρ(g−1x)/ρ(x).

Induction assumes AC, an LCH group, a closed subgroup, and a strongly continuous unitary subgroup representation. Covariance is F(xh)=σ(h)−1F(x), and compact support refers to the descended quotient norm.

For equivalent Radon measures on an arbitrary homogeneous quotient, Radon–Nikodym densities are selected on disjoint open sigma-compact pieces. The comparison is assembled componentwise; no global Borel density is asserted.

load_bearing.statement: For every n≥0 and λ⊢n, the stated adjacent-column Garnir relation holds integrally and after reduction to every field; every polytabloid straightens over Z to standard polytabloids; these form a Z-basis of the integral Specht module and an F-basis over every field F.

Assume AC. If H is closed in an LCH group G, then G/H is LCH and the quotient map is open. Every compact quotient subset has a compact lift covering it, and THf(xH)=∫H f(xh)dh maps Cc(G) onto Cc(G/H).

Assume AC. For a countable p-chain started at b, μb(y)=EbΣ0≤n<Tb+ 1{Xn=y} satisfies μb(b)=1 and Σy μb(y)=EbTb+. It is invariant away from b, its flow into b is Pb(Tb+<∞), and it is pointwise minimal among nonnegative solutions normalized to one at b and invariant away from b. If b is recurrent, μbp=μb.
Assume AC. For fixed left Haar measures and any rho-function, there is a unique full-support Radon measure μρ on G/H satisfying ∫G fρ dx=∫G/H ∫H f(xh)dh dμρ(xH) for every f∈Cc(G).
Assume AC. For an irreducible countable transition matrix with invariant probability π, every b satisfies π(b)>0, EbTb+=1/π(b), and μb(y)=π(y)/π(b) for every y.

For finite-dimensional complex V and n≥0, the natural map End(V)⊗n→End(V⊗n) is an equivariant linear isomorphism. Invariant tensors are spanned both by T⊗n and by g⊗n for invertible g; their image is EndSn(V⊗n), which also equals the unital algebra generated by the place-sum operators Δ(T). This includes V=0.
For n≥0 and λ,μ⊢n over C, the restrictions to Sλ of the row-orbit homomorphisms attached to semistandard λ-fillings of content μ span HomSn(Sλ,Mμ).

Assume AC. The sections ξf,v(x)=∫H f(xh)σ(h)v dh, for f∈Cc(G) and v∈V, lie in the continuous covariant model. Their finite span is uniformly dense on compact quotient supports, and the completion equals locally strongly measurable covariant L2 sections modulo quotient almost-everywhere equality.

Assume AC. For an irreducible positive-recurrent countable p with invariant probability π and Σy π(y)|f(y)|<∞, n−1Σk<n f(Xk)→Σy π(y)f(y) almost surely under every deterministic-start law Px. Complex f is handled componentwise; aperiodicity is unnecessary.

Assume AC. For closed L≤H≤G and compatible rho-functions and Weil measures, rx(hL)=ρGL(xh)/(ρGH(xh)ρHL(h)) is positive continuous, and ∫G/L φ dμGL=∫G/H ∫H/L φ(xhL)rx(hL)dμHL dμGH for every φ∈Cc(G/L). The inner integral is independent of the representative x.

concerns.concern: The final sentence says a periodic chain may have “p^{(n)}(x,·)=π for all n when the initial law is already stationary.” This confuses a deterministic-start transition row with the law πp^{(n)}. In the displayed two-cycle, every deterministic-start row remains a point mass; at n=0 the asserted equality already requires δx=π.

The first remark says “Any other fixed order of the same corners would give a different chain with the same quotient multiset.” Arbitrarily reordering the prescribed corner spans need not give submodules. In the owned characteristic-two example λ=(2,1), starting with the lower corner gives span{v3+v1}; (12) sends its generator to v3+v2, outside that span.

Two remarks are false as written: “one countably infinite layer for each n” contradicts the finite set of partitions of each fixed n; and “Adjacency ... is therefore not mere containment of diagrams of neighbouring sizes” is false for genuine Young diagrams. If [λ]⊂[ν] and |ν|=|λ|+1, the unique extra box is addable by definition. The example only shows that an arbitrary proposed box need not produce a Young diagram.

The dominance remark correctly states support on λ dominating μ, then reverses this in “Specht modules of shapes dominated by μ.” The owned example M^(2,1) contains S^(3), and (3) dominates (2,1), not conversely.

Steps 3.1 and 6.1 construct a stationary reverse chain using F2–F3, but those suppliers establish stationarity and finite-dimensional laws for a supplied chain, not existence of one. The opened cor-canonical-markov-chain-on-path-space supplies exactly the needed existence under AC; that application is omitted.

Step 2.4 says a matrix-unit commutator is “a matrix unit or 0”; [E12,E21]=E11−E22 instead requires distributing a sum of shorter words. Steps 5.1–6.1 also order eigenvalues written as arbitrary complex scalars without first proving they are real. The elementary tensor basis makes each Δ(Ess) diagonal with nonnegative integer eigenvalues, which supplies the missing justification.

Step 3.1 establishes the averaging bound for continuous W supported in a common compact set, then concludes their averages converge to the pointwise measurable average A(U)=FQ. It does not explicitly identify the bounded L2 extension with pointwise fiber integration on measurable Bochner functions. The stated Weil supplier covers Cc functions and the compact-kernel supplier covers continuous kernels; a compact-support measurable extension or equivalent identification argument is needed here. The continuous-model density proof is separate and does not resolve this step.

The equivariance paragraph says the target carries its action by restriction from Sn and that “both modules are Sn-modules.” The deletion shape has size n−1, and its defined tabloid module naturally carries an S(n−1) action. No Sn action on that target has been defined.

Statement clause 3 describes the deletion-shape Specht module’s action as “obtained by restriction along S_{n-1}⊂Sn.” Its defined action is already the natural S(n−1) action; no ambient Sn action on this size-(n−1) module is supplied. The proof’s deletion-equivariance calculation uses the correct natural action.
The diagonal-action composition display starts with (g′h)⊗n but its right side applies g′ to gv_i and ends with g′⊗n composed with g⊗n. The variables in this equality do not match.

Step 1.5 defines m(v) only for nonzero v, then asserts m(v−cSθS(e_t0))<m(v) without allowing the remainder to be zero. For v=θS(e_t0), the remainder is zero. Later termination reasoning intends the alternative “zero or strictly lower level.”
Statement clause 4 says a vector ψ “equals μ=λ and lies in Cφ.” The vector and weight tuple are different types; the intended conclusions, proved later, are μ=λ and ψ∈Cφ.

The Given paragraph calls the three displayed partitions of 3 “the four partitions.” Step 4.1 says “all spaces here are three-dimensional,” although the example explicitly has summands of dimensions one and two. These audit sentences contradict its correct enumeration and dimension calculation.

The first remark says “Each of its three rows is a column” for shape (1,1,1). The diagram has three one-box rows and one column of height three; the following antisymmetrization argument uses that single column.
